source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: Silage (fermented feed) helps pigs get protein-rich leaves through the dry season, when fresh leaves are hardest to find. Leaf silage alone (using fodder-tree leaves such as gliricidia, sesbania, and leucaena) is generally more palatable to pigs than 'complete' silage mixed with grains and tubers — a well-liked recipe combines gliricidia, sesbania, and leucaena leaves at roughly 20:30:50, though other ratios also work; younger gliricidia leaves are more palatable than older, tougher ones, and leucaena should never exceed 15% of the total diet since it can be toxic in larger amounts. To make silage: chop leaves, stems, and vines into small pieces; weigh each ingredient; mix together (pouring over rice bran or maize if using a complete-silage recipe); spray with EM4 (effective microorganism starter) and mix gently; pack tightly into a plastic bag inside a sealed container, pressing out all air; and leave to ferment for at least 14 days before opening and checking for mould before feeding. Introduce silage to pigs gradually, since not all pigs take to it immediately.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
